A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, A Generalization Theory for Zero-Shot Prediction. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original Gaussian simulations and zero-shot image-classification experiments in Figures 2–4, with experimental details in Appendix F.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original simulation and image-classification results in Figures 2–4, supported by Appendix F.

M1.justification: The conditional-mean and information-density approaches, SSL objectives, and prediction procedures are unchanged. Appendix D.5 adds a mathematical description of existing template prompting without introducing a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian binary-classification simulation, pretraining sources, and image-classification coverage: DTD, Flowers 102, FGVC Aircraft, SUN397, ImageNet-1k, and ImageNet-Captions.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains Direct, Indirect, CLIP, and VICReg. Figures 3–4 retain the same template-versus-unbiased and template-versus-CuPL comparisons across ResNet-50, NLLB-CLIP, and ViT-B/32.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F retain the same splits, top-k accuracy metrics, prompting budgets, and model settings. The simulation still uses 10,000 pretraining observations, 500 prompts, and 30 training epochs. Appendix D.5 does not report an experimental protocol change.

E4.justification: The residual-dependence sweep in Figure 2 and prompt-count analyses in Figures 3–4 are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or empirical supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Figure 2 continues to report standard errors from 10 seeds, while Figures 3–4 report standard deviations across 10 prompt-sampling seeds. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: Figures 2–4 retain identical curves and error bars, and their reported findings are unchanged. Appendix F.3 retains ImageNet-1k accuracies of 28.11%, 33.51%, and 32.81% for ResNet-50, NLLB-CLIP, and ViT-B/32, respectively.

T1.justification: Appendix D.5 adds the structural equation Z = f(Y,U), the independence condition between templates U and labels Y, and an explicit empirical prompt measure. Appendix C also makes the infinity norm explicit in two proof steps. The main theorem statements and convergence rates are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same claims about population prediction targets, prompt bias, residual dependence, estimation error, and finite-sample guarantees.

C2.justification: Appendix D.5 expands v1's statement that templates have no relationship with labels: v2 explains that independence concerns the unfilled template U, while the completed caption Z can depend on Y through label insertion. Empirical interpretations and existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The reported implementation and reproducibility information remains unchanged, including hardware, model tags, generation settings, preprocessing, training hyperparameters, and code and prompt-access information. Appendix D.5's addition formalizes the existing prompting strategy.

R1.justification: The cited works, comparisons with previous theory, and novelty positioning are unchanged. Several citations receive punctuation and parenthesis corrections without adding or removing research references.

P1.justification: V2 adds a focused explanation in Appendix D.5 and makes scattered grammar, spelling, and citation-format corrections. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: All five figures and the existing table designs are retained. Appendix text and page breaks shift, including the model-specification table moving lower on page 58 and the prompt-generator description moving to page 59.

improvement.justification: Appendix D.5 resolves a localized ambiguity by distinguishing label-independent templates from label-dependent completed captions and specifying their empirical distribution. Explicit infinity-norm notation and small editorial corrections further improve precision. These are useful, limited improvements; the main theoretical and empirical findings remain unchanged.
